new_jobs.description:
Machine Learning Engineer | AI Security & Fraud Detection

Location:
San Francisco, CA - Onsite
Compensation:
$180,000–$260,000 Base + Equity (Flexible up to $300,000 for Exceptional Candidates)
Experience:
3+ Years, Ideally 5+ Years
Industry:
AI Infrastructure, Agentic AI, Cybersecurity, Fraud Prevention

About the Opportunity

Shields Group Search is partnering with a well-funded, early-stage AI infrastructure startup building the trust and security layer for the rapidly emerging AI agent economy.
As AI agents increasingly act autonomously on behalf of individuals and businesses, from booking services and accessing APIs to executing financial transactions, companies need infrastructure that can determine which agents are legitimate, who they represent, what actions they're authorized to perform, and whether their behavior presents a security or fraud risk.
Our client is building real-time verification and decisioning infrastructure that enables businesses to safely interact with AI agents at scale.
The platform combines agent identity verification, behavioral intelligence, risk assessment, and security controls to distinguish legitimate automated activity from suspicious or malicious behavior.

We're looking for an exceptional Machine Learning Engineer to build the models that distinguish a trusted AI agent from an attack, in real time and under load.

This is an opportunity to join a small, highly technical founding-stage engineering team and take meaningful ownership of mission-critical ML infrastructure.
What You'll Be Working On
The models behind this platform operate directly on the production request path. They must evaluate activity and support trust decisions in real time, under the same strict latency constraints as the rest of the infrastructure.
There is no offline batch job to hide behind and no second chance if a prediction is too slow or incorrect.

You'll work on problems involving:

Real-Time Fraud & Threat Detection:
Develop ML models that identify potentially fraudulent, malicious, or unauthorized agent activity while minimizing false positives.
Behavioral & Anomaly Detection:
Identify suspicious patterns, anomalous agent interactions, and emerging risks across automated transactions and API activity.
Low-Latency ML Inference:
Build and optimize production model-serving systems capable of making accurate decisions under demanding latency and throughput requirements.
Cold-Start & Low-Label Learning:
Develop effective detection approaches when labeled examples are scarce, including unsupervised learning, weak supervision, and custom evaluation datasets.
End-to-End ML Ownership:
Build, evaluate, deploy, monitor, and continuously improve production ML systems, from data and feature pipelines through real-time serving.
Adversarial ML:
Help build systems that remain effective as malicious actors adapt their behavior to evade detection.
Agentic AI Infrastructure:
Work at the intersection of modern ML, AI agents, tool calling, identity verification, and security.

What We're Looking For

Must-Haves

3+ years of professional ML experience
, ideally 5+ years, building, evaluating, and deploying production models, not just research or notebooks.
Strong Python and a modern ML framework (PyTorch or TensorFlow); solid SQL.
Production ML systems end to end: feature pipelines, training, evaluation, and low-latency, real-time serving.

We have working models: code that takes in an MRI series and produces measurements surgeons care
about. We need an engineer to turn them into production systems that are tested, versioned, deployed
and monitored, with every output traceable to the model, code and data that produced it. This is an
MLOps-focused role: reproducibility, versioning, deployment and monitoring of our models are the core
of the job.

An implementation partner is currently standing up our core platform: Databricks, MLflow, our
databases and model serving. You'll work alongside them during the build, take ownership when they
hand it over, and be the person who gets our models onto it and keeps them running. You'll also help
grow and connect the data our research depends on.

This is a hands-on engineering role on a small team. You'll work closely with our Principal AI/ML Engineer
on how models are built, tracked, released and served.

What you'll work on in your first year

Take our models from prototype to production.
Refactor MVP model code, starting with our MRI

imaging pipeline, into tested, typed, reproducible Python packages. Find out what's slow and make it
fast.
Make every result reproducible and traceable.
Register models in MLflow with pinned code,

environment and data versions. Build batch and online inference on Databricks so that every stored
output records the model that produced it. Define how a new model is validated, promoted and
rolled back, and write those procedures down.
Build the path from research code to production.
Set up project templates, CI, code review

and a clear path from "my model works" to "my model is registered and deployable" for everyone on
the team who writes model code.
Grow and connect our research data.
Our core research datasets already exist. You'll help shape

how they need to grow and change as we do, and connect our data sources (imaging, annotations,
scanner and protocol metadata, clinical outcomes) so researchers can find, query and use them.
That includes designing schemas, versioning the datasets our models are trained and evaluated on,
and writing loaders that handle the edge cases real-world data throws at you.
Own the platform.
Once our partner hands it over, you'll run it day to day: CI/CD, access, cost and

upgrades. You'll also set up monitoring for the services and for data and model drift, so we find out
about problems before our users do.

What we're looking for

2+ years of professional software engineering, mostly in Python, writing tested code that runs in

production.
You've taken at least one ML system from prototype to production yourself and kept it running

afterward, so you know what breaks.
A working understanding of how models are trained and evaluated, enough to reproduce a training

run: seeds, nondeterministic GPU operations, data splits, preprocessing versions. Experience with
PyTorch.
Hands-on MLOps: experiment tracking or a model registry (MLflow or similar), deploying model

inference, and CI/CD.
Data engineering: you've built pipelines that produce datasets other people train on. Relational

database design in PostgreSQL or similar: schemas, migrations, constraints, and knowing when not
to normalize.
You've reviewed other people's code and helped less experienced developers write better software

without slowing them down.
You've worked at a startup or on a small team where you owned work end to end.
You can take a loosely defined problem, ask the right questions, and come back with a working

solution without needing step-by-step direction.

Nice to have

Databricks (strongly preferred): Unity Catalog, Delta Lake, Spark, Model Serving, Workflows.
Medical imaging experience: DICOM, MRI or CT pipelines, de-identification.
Longitudinal clinical or outcomes data, including follow-up and censored time-to-event data.
Regulated healthcare software: HIPAA and handling patient data, FDA software as a medical device,

design controls.
Azure (blob storage, Entra ID) or another major cloud.
Building and deploying APIs (FastAPI or similar).
Storing and compressing vectors: pgvector, quantization, dimensionality reduction.
Speeding up numerical Python code (NumPy, PyTorch, GPUs).
Side projects you've built and shipped on your own.

What this role is not

Not primarily a research or modeling role.
Your main job is making our models reproducible and

reliable in production, and building the data they're trained on. You'll need to understand our
models, and because we're a small team you may contribute to research from time to time, but it
won't be the core of the role.
Not building a platform from scratch, or tuning one component of a large system.
Our core

infrastructure is being stood up now. Your job is to own it and put our work on it, across the stack.

new_jobs.title: Embedded Software Engineer
new_jobs.description:
About the Company

We engineer connectivity and embedded compute solutions that power connected devices worldwide. With decades of experience, our solutions are secure by design, globally compliant and supported over long lifecycles.

About the Role

The Embedded Software Engineer designs, develops, and supports Wi-Fi radio firmware and driver software for Ezurio's wireless connectivity products, working closely with the RF hardware development team in the USA and Taiwan, program management, and customers to deliver reliable, innovative, and resilient embedded software. The ideal candidate is comfortable working close to the metal - register-level access, bootloaders, and drivers in a resource-constrained environment - as well as building the connectivity stacks that sit above them, and brings strong debugging and root-cause analysis skills to complex hardware/software and RF interaction issues. Deep 802.11 protocol expertise is not required; we are willing to train a strong embedded/RTOS candidate on the Wi-Fi-specific pieces. Experience developing software for network protocols (Wi-Fi, TCP/IP, or similar) is a useful plus. This role is preferably based in hybrid work arrangement in Akron, Ohio. Remote candidates will also be considered. Legal authorization to work in the US is required.

Responsibilities

Wi-Fi Radio Firmware Development

Design, develop, and maintain firmware for Wi-Fi radio subsystems, including MAC/PHY interfacing, calibration routines, and channel/RF management.
Bring up Wi-Fi silicon on new hardware platforms: port and validate vendor SDKs, drivers, and radio calibration data for new designs.
Develop and maintain radio firmware within an RTOS environment (e.g., ThreadX or similar) and host-side Wi-Fi drivers under Linux, with real-time scheduling, interrupt handling, and register-level access to radio and host interfaces (SDIO, PCIe, USB, DMA).
Write clean, well-documented, testable code following Ezurio coding standards and secure development practices.
Support 802.11 protocol-layer behavior (association, authentication, power-save, rate adaptation) and power management/wake-on-wireless design in coordination with vendor stacks.

Debug, Test & Quality

Debug complex RF firmware issues using tools such on hardware where on-device debug access (e.g., JTAG/debug ports) is limited, using debug output, code analysis, logic analyzers, oscilloscopes, and Wi-Fi packet capture tools (e.g., Wireshark) and JTAG/SWD
Develop and execute unit, functional, integration, and system-level tests; work with SWQA teams to contribute to test infrastructure and CI/CD pipelines.
Reproduce, isolate, and resolve field and customer-reported Wi-Fi issues (throughput, roaming, association drops, coexistence) and drive issues to root cause and closure.
Participate in code reviews and enforce quality gates across the software development lifecycle.

Cross-Functional & Customer Collaboration

Partner with the RF hardware team (USA and Taiwan) during schematic review, antenna design, and prototype bring-up to flag firmware-relevant design considerations early.
Work directly with customers and program managers to clarify Wi-Fi firmware requirements, scope, and acceptance criteria for co-development programs.
Support manufacturing, NPI, and DVT/PVT activities with RF test tools, calibration procedures, and production-line firmware as needed.
Provide clear technical status updates to program managers and contribute to schedule and risk discussions.

Documentation & Process

Produce and maintain technical documentation: design specifications, API references, porting guides, and release notes.
Maintain source control hygiene, branching strategy, and release/versioning discipline across active programs.
Contribute to the continuous improvement of embedded software development practices within the Custom SOM & SBC group.

Qualifications

Strong proficiency in C working in embedded, memory-constrained, real-time systems.
Solid understanding of processor architecture, memory management, and real-time constraints in embedded systems and working with register access.
Proven debugging skills across the hardware/software boundary, using debug output, JTAG/SWD, oscilloscopes, logic analyzers, and ideally Wi-Fi packet capture tools.
Demonstrated persistence and rigor in debugging and driving issues to true root cause rather than applying surface-level fixes.
Ability to read schematics and datasheets, and to communicate effectively with RF hardware engineers on radio and interface details.
Strong written and verbal communication skills; comfortable presenting technical status to customers and internal stakeholders.
Effective collaborator in a fast-paced, globally distributed team environment (coordinating with the RF hardware team in the USA and Taiwan), able to manage multiple concurrent programs.
Ideally hand-on RTOS experience: task scheduling, interrupt handling, and priority management in a resource-constrained system. Note that specific RTOS experience e.g. ThreadX, Zephyr, or similar matters less than a working understanding of RTOS concepts and real hands-on time in one.
Working knowledge of Linux (kernel modules, device drivers, kernel/user-space interfaces) is a plus, since our Wi-Fi drivers run under Linux.
Experience with host interfaces such as SDIO, PCIe, or USB is most relevant; familiarity with SPI, I2C, and UART is also useful.
Exposure to 802.11 MAC-layer concepts (association, authentication, power-save, rate adaptation) is a plus; we will train a strong embedded/RTOS candidate who doesn't yet have this.
Working knowledge of version control (Git), CI/CD pipelines, and issue tracking tools such as Jira.
Chipset vendor SDK exposure is a plus: Cypress/Infineon, NXP, Qualcomm/Atheros (QCA) or similar Wi-Fi silicon vendors.
Familiarity with RF/PHY concepts (calibration, gain control, channel switching) is a plus.
Prior experience with another wireless or networking protocol stacks e.g. Bluetooth, Zigbee, Thread, Cellular is valuable even without direct Wi-Fi background.
Power management firmware experience (sleep states, wake-on-wireless) is a plus, especially for battery-powered or IoT platforms.

Education/Experience

Bachelor's degree in Computer Engineering, Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, or a related technical field. Equivalent professional experience considered in lieu of degree.
5+ years of embedded software or firmware development experience in an electronics design and manufacturing environment.
Direct experience with Wi-Fi or other wireless radio firmware/driver bring-up is strongly preferred; we will train a strong embedded/RTOS candidate without direct Wi-Fi background.
Experience supporting customer co-development programs (NRE-based or joint development agreements) is a plus.
Experience with wireless certification, RF coexistence, or low-power design considerations is a plus.
This role is based in Akron, OH on a hybrid schedule with at least weekly in-office presence, to support close collaboration with the RF hardware and QA teams. Fully remote work will be considered on a case-by-case basis for exceptional candidates with deep Wi-Fi radio chip experience (e.g., QCA, Infineon, NXP).

We're an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, or status as a protected veteran.

Work with vendors and the Media Engineering team to define clear requirements, deploy media-processing changes, and identify and resolve defects.
Work independently and collaboratively, with transparency, autonomy, and a commitment to quality in assignments of every size.

Experience with web technologies, digital video workflows and operations, and video technology development

Job Description

As an Advanced Test Engineer here at Honeywell Aerospace, you will play a pivotal role in advancing the quality and reliability of aerospace products through innovative test engineering practices. You will lead the development and execution of sophisticated test plans and procedures, leveraging cutting-edge methodologies to ensure our aerospace solutions meet the highest standards of performance and safety.

You will report directly to our Engineering Manager, and you’ll work out of our Richardson, TX location on a 9/80 work schedule.

In this role, you will impact the aerospace industry by ensuring that Honeywell’s aerospace products are rigorously tested and validated, contributing to safer and more efficient air travel worldwide. Delivering mission-critical, electronic solutions that protect lives. Use your creativity and critical thinking to take our products from concept to customer. You will lead the development and execution of sophisticated test solutions for Monolithic Microwave Integrated Circuits (MMICs). This role involves analyzing detailed test requirements and designing advanced Automated Test Equipment (ATE) systems tailored to customer specifications. The engineer will create and implement comprehensive test strategies, including test plans, acceptance procedures, and rigorous design verification processes.

The position requires leadership in enhancing team test capabilities through planning, coordination, and development of custom test equipment, including fixture design and fabrication. Responsibilities include performing RF test setup, calibration, validation, and troubleshooting of complex assemblies to ensure accurate, repeatable measurements.

The engineer will develop and maintain automated test software using National Instruments LabVIEW, integrating instrumentation and databases to enable scalable, efficient, and high-throughput testing environments. Additional duties include conducting advanced troubleshooting, failure analysis, and root cause investigations for MMIC devices and RF assemblies, as well as executing product qualification and environmental stress testing to meet industry standards.

This role also involves generating detailed technical reports, managing test data systems, and supporting laboratory operations such as asset tracking and equipment maintenance. Precision work under microscopes for inspection, assembly support, and failure analysis are also required. The ideal candidate is highly technical, detail-oriented, and capable of working independently in a fast-paced engineering environment.

Responsibilities

Design and maintain automated test software for ATE systems using LabVIEW, Python, C, C++, Visual Basic and other industry-standard test development tools to improve efficiency and data integrity
Analyze customer specifications to define test requirements, configurations, and acceptance criteria for MMIC testing
Develop and implement comprehensive test plans, including ATE configurations, fixtures, and software/hardware interfaces
Perform RF characterization of MMIC/semiconductor testing devices, including S-parameters, output power, noise figure, and two-tone measurements
Set up, calibrate, and execute RF test systems and on-wafer probe testing using appropriate standards
Troubleshoot and diagnose complex RF circuits independently using strong microwave theory knowledge
Conduct statistical analysis and generate detailed technical reports on test results and performance
Manage laboratory operations, including test databases, equipment calibration, asset tracking, and vendor procurement support

Qualifications

YOU MUST HAVE

Bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution in a technical discipline such as science, technology, engineering, mathematics
Minimum of 5 years of RF experience specific with ATE for RF/Microwave and components including the development and testing of components, experience in building rack & stack test equipment.
Minimum of 3years of test software development including LabVIEW, Python, MSQL, C, C++
Minimum of 2 years of experience in manufacturing or in a high-tech electronics industry.
Minimum of 2 years of using Microsoft Office Suite including SharePoint and Excel.

WE VALUE

Bachelor’s degree in engineering or a related field or equivalent education and experience.
Experience developing ATE software and operating RF test equipment, including wafer probe stations, VNAs, oscilloscopes, spectrum analyzers, signal generators, power supplies, and RF calibration standards
Strong RF characterization expertise for GaN/GaAs MMICs, including S-parameters, large-signal, two-tone, and stability testing through Ka-band
Proficiency interpreting schematics, technical drawings, and applying core electronics and microwave theory fundamentals
Hands-on experience with RF test fixtures, PCB design, and assembly, including wire bonding of MMIC devices for test readiness
Ability to perform precision work under a microscope with sub-micron geometries
Familiarity with DoD/military qualification and testing standards
Strong collaboration skills with the ability to work cross-functionally while also operating independently with accountability and initiative
Demonstrated adaptability, problem-solving, and continuous improvement mindset, with strong organizational and time management skills in dynamic environments

Us Person Requirements

Due to compliance with U.S. export control laws and regulations, candidate must be a U.S. person, which is defined as, a U.S. citizen, a U.S. permanent resident, or have protected status in the U.S. under asylum or refugee status.

Benefits

Beyond a performance-driven salary, you'll work alongside dedicated experts on technology that's advancing aviation. As a Honeywell Aerospace employee, you're eligible for a comprehensive benefits package that includes:

Employer-subsidized medical, dental, vision and life insurance
Short-term and long-term disability coverage
401(k) match, flexible spending accounts and health savings accounts
Employee assistance program and educational assistance
Parental leave and 12 paid holidays
Paid time off for vacation, personal and sick time

Our new brand identity pairs that heritage with real momentum, as we build technology that helps pilots navigate with confidence, aircraft operate more efficiently, and operators stay ahead of change. to perform design, development, and hardware/software integration in Arlington, VA for the Electronic Warfare Division

Our division primarily focuses on research & development and advanced prototyping, transforming state of the art signal processing algorithms into real-time software systems
.

Projects involve small multi-disciplinary teams of engineers working together in spiral or agile development environments to meet aggressive customer schedules aimed at near-term field demonstrations. Join a team of experts in implementing high-performance signal processing on general purpose processors, such as ARM.

The Successful Candidate Will Support

Contributing to design and development of advanced systems as a part of multi-disciplinary teams. These teams are made up of other software team members and subject matter experts from the areas of systems engineering, hardware, firmware, machine learning, RF front end design, and signal processing.
Designing, implementing, and testing real-time C/C++ software for multi-core systems running Linux or a real-time operating systems, such as VxWorks
Build software products that utilize third party mathematics and communication libraries
Interface communication standards / protocols such as TCP/IP, UDP, and DDS
Read and understand signal processing algorithms written in MATLAB
Work with Linux operating system as well as experience with real-time operating systems

Documenting the developed systems
Support system field testing and collection events, usually about a week in duration once or twice a year

new_jobs.title: Data Scientist and AI Developer Intern
new_jobs.description:
At Daiichi Sankyo, we are united by a single purpose, to improve lives around the world through innovative medicines. With a legacy of innovation since 1899, a presence in more than 30 countries, and more than 19,000 employees, we are advancing breakthrough therapies in oncology, cardiovascular disease, rare diseases, and immune disorders. Guided by our 2030 vision to "be an innovative global healthcare company contributing to the sustainable development of society", we are shaping a healthier, more hopeful future for patients, their families, and society.

Job Summary

We are currently seeking a Data Scientist and AI Developer Intern from June 2027 – May 2028. This position works for approximately 37.5 hours per week in the summer and 20 hours per week for the remainder of the internship.

The intern will be accountable for ideating, designing, developing, and supporting applications and solutions to explore various machine intelligence techniques including but not limited to natural language processing (NLP), predictive analysis using supervised and unsupervised machine learning (ML), and generative AI (GenAI) using large language models (LLM) for use cases that focus on data quality and data governance. The role may also involve working with cloud technologies and services such as AWS and GCP to support scalable data processing, AI/ML experimentation, application deployment, and integration with enterprise data platforms. The position requires familiarity with AI/ML/NLP/GenAI techniques, SQL databases and data manipulation, API architectures, cloud-based services, and user interface development. Strong work ethic and eagerness and ability to self-learn is critical.

Responsibilities

Design, develop, and support AI/ML/NLP/GenAI solutions.
Analyze data using SQL and other techniques.
Extract data using REST APIs.
Develop and support simple user interfaces.
Support development, deployment, and integration of cloud-based data and AI solutions using technologies such as AWS and GCP.
Create simple visualization.
Assist in various other related functions such as preparing documentation, taking meeting notes, plan and manage work, make presentations, etc.
Augment knowledge with self-driven learning.

Qualifications

Qualified candidates must have completed bachelor’s degree in computer science, data analytics or a related discipline. Experience with SQL development, data analysis using MS Excel, developing simple web portals and machine learning (NLP, predictive analytics) is required. Prior academic or professional work experience is preferred; experience in the pharmaceutical industry and/or with clinical data is a plus. Enthusiasm, eagerness to learn and take on responsibilities, and teamwork are essential qualities.

Daiichi Sankyo, Inc. is an equal opportunity/affirmative action employer. Qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, race, color, religion, national origin, disability, protected veteran status, age, or any other characteristic protected by law.
